object: rock graffito over a rock shelf, above a rude drawing of a man carrying a staff or flower
site: Dakka: isolated table-shaped hill south of Gebel Abu Dirwa, three miles south-west of the temple (Lower Nubia), east side of the hill
notes: Rock graffito in archaic style, one of three found by O. Bates (Archaeological Survey of Nubia, Bulletin 5); Griffith's hand-copies of November 1910 and Firth's photographs (Pls. XI, XII). The letter in rem is Griffith's sub-number (91 a, b, c); REM's own form of the suffix was not checked. Griffith: 'apparently a proper name, Shaqeshakin'; he prints '?' before the last two signs (l, o). A sign is 9.5 cm high. The type is letter-spaced; written as one word after Griffith's analysis.
